A foreign citizen was beaten to death by a group of around 50 people during a protest march in South Africa’s east coast city of Durban, police said Thursday, as anti-immigrant tensions continue to flare in Africa’s most advanced economy.
Police said the group approached the man, who was standing at the side of a road during a march through the streets of Durban’s city center, and assaulted him.

France on Thursday reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.
It is suspected that the victim was bitten by a midge carrying the virus in eastern France where it had circulated among animals this spring and summer, the government said in a statement.

After a lifetime spent shadowing wildlife on the plains of Kenya’s Amboseli National Park, Eric Ole Kesoi’s reputation as one of the Maasai’s finest trackers is built on his ability to know where to look. At the end of this search, however, it takes all of his conviction to keep his eyes on the sight before him.
At the center of the grisly scene are the gnawed remains of a young cow, peppered with bite wounds made by the pride of lions that lie writhing and panting a few feet away, fighting for their lives. Nine blue-stained tongues loll from foaming mouths, the calling card of an unseen weapon.
“Poisoning is really the most brutal form of killing an animal. It’s heart wrenching,” Kesoi tells CNN.
